comment: Formation tuning (docs/design/FORMATION_CONTRACT.md 2). Read by the Training Ground simulator / tuner and by the C++ rules. Angles are relative to the leader's heading (or to the wall's outward normal for wall.*), positive = right (UE yaw). The tuner changes only value, inside min..max.

slot.side_offset.doc: Diamond / wedge: sideways distance of the side men from the leader.

slot.back_offset.doc: Diamond / wedge: distance of the side men behind the leader.

slot.min_spacing.doc: Two members closer than this count as a spacing failure.

diamond.rear_back.doc: Diamond: the rear man straight behind the leader.

pair.side_offset.doc: Pair (2 members): the partner to the right of the leader.

pair.back_offset.doc: Pair (2 members): the partner behind the leader.

pair.scan_period.doc: Pair (2 members): one full sweep cycle of the partner (3 -> 6 -> 9 and back).

pair.scan_from.doc: Pair: the partner's sweep starts here (90 = 3 o'clock); the sweep runs clockwise through 180 (6 o'clock) to pair.scan_to.

pair.scan_to.doc: Pair: the partner's sweep ends here (270 = 9 o'clock), written above 180 so the arc runs through 6 o'clock.

triad.rear_back.doc: v2.2: the triad's rear man Z straight behind the leader (walks backwards looking at 6).

column.base_back.doc: Column: the first follower behind the leader.

column.stagger.doc: Column herringbone: alternate followers this far right / left of the axis.

column.stagger_clear.doc: v2.3 (red team #7): the trail column's stagger aside shrinks until the slot keeps this from every wall surface (agent radius 35 + 10).

column.side_deg.doc: Wide column (herringbone): right / left followers look this far off the heading.

column.narrow_width.doc: v1.1 (user Q1 = A): a column in a passage narrower than this uses the narrow sectors (P forward over the shoulder, L back at a slant).

column.narrow_fwd_deg.doc: Narrow column: P looks this far right of the heading (forward over the leader's shoulder).

column.narrow_back_deg.doc: Narrow column: L looks back at a slant, this far LEFT of the heading (-value).

line.fan_inner.doc: Line: the two inner members fan out this far.

line.fan_outer.doc: Line: the two outer members fan out this far.

echelon.step.doc: Echelon: each next member this far back and this far to the open side.

echelon.sector_lead.doc: Echelon: the leader looks this far to the open side.

echelon.sector_2.doc: Echelon: the second member's sector centre (open side).

echelon.sector_3.doc: Echelon: the third member's sector centre (open side).

echelon.sector_4.doc: Echelon: the last member's sector centre (open side, rear; user Q2 = A: 150 keeps 5-7 o'clock watched).

blizzard.back_offset.doc: Blizzard tight diamond: side men behind the leader; the rear man at twice this.

hedgehog.radius.doc: Hedgehog: members this far from the centre, facing out.

wall.spacing.doc: Wall layout: shoulder-to-shoulder spacing along the wall.

wall.face_offset.doc: Wall layout: the body centre this far off the wall face.

wall.flank_deg.doc: Wall layout: flank men look this far off the outward normal (L +, P -: 8 / 4 o'clock).

wall.neighbour_deg.doc: Wall layout, 4 members: the 4th man's neighbour turns to the centre (5 / 7 o'clock).

wall.end_deg.doc: Wall layout, 4 members: the 4th man at the end looks along the wall (3-4 / 8-9 o'clock).

wall_end.probe_dist.doc: v2.4 (user bug report 2026-10-26): the wall layout's open-arc coverage probes a ring this far round the group (FormationWallRules.EndLooks, bot check 13).

wall_end.cover_pct.doc: v2.4: the wall layout's looks must hold this share of the open probe ring; below it (a wall END: flanks round the end open) the looks are spread over the open arc. Also bot check 13's bar.

approach.arrive_dist.doc: v2.5 (user rule 2026-10-26, the covered approach to the wall): a member is at the wall within this of his wall slot - he takes his layout look (the runner: along the wall); the approach ends when everyone is in (FormationWallRules.Approach, bot check 14).

slide.max_off_wall.doc: v2.2 wall slide (user 2026-10-25): a destination this close to the surface of the wall the squad stands at (on its side, along it) is a slide - the squad moves sideways together, no re-forming.

slide.lead_out_deg.doc: v2.2: the leading / trailing end look along the wall turned this far outward.

pace.patrol.doc: Patrol (walk) pace of the whole squad relative to the walk speed (user 2026-10-25: ~80 %, kept - variant A).

move.backward_mult.doc: A member walking backwards moves at most this fraction of the walk speed (user 2026-10-25, variant A: 0.9 > the 0.8 patrol pace, so the rear man keeps up).

move.catchup_mult.doc: A member far behind his slot may move this much faster than the squad pace.

facing.turn_speed.doc: Body turn rate (Godot lerp_angle turn_speed, FacingRules::StepYaw).

scan.period.doc: Patrol scan: one full sweep cycle of the side men.

scan.center_side.doc: Patrol scan: centre of the side men's sweep (P +, L -).

scan.amp_side.doc: Patrol scan: half-width of the side men's sweep (45 = 12 -> 3).

scan.amp_lead.doc: Patrol scan: the leader's search half-width (v1.2: 30 = 11-1 o'clock, as the design says).

scan.dwell_exp.doc: Patrol scan: dwell shaping (sign(s)*|s|^exp; 1 = plain sine, lower = longer holds at the ends).

halt.side_deg.doc: Short halt: the side men hold this sector centre (2 / 10 o'clock).

rear.share_half.doc: v2.2 (user 2026-10-25): the rear guard searches 6 o'clock +- this on the move (5-7 o'clock); he guarantees his cone minus it.

rear.wall_shift_deg.doc: v2.2: with walls on ONE side of the rear guard (within look.wall_dist) his share turns this far towards the open side (wall left -> ~5 o'clock).

coverage.max_sweep.doc: v2.2: largest sweep amplitude of a member covering his share (the triad's P: 3 -> 12 -> 9).

coverage.max_gap_deg.doc: v2.2 check 10: the largest uncovered open arc allowed (>= 90 % of patrol time).

look.wall_dist.doc: v2.1.1 (user 6A): a wall surface closer than this blocks looks towards it (FormationSectorRules.ClearLook) - 60 cm beyond the wall-stare check's 200 so a man turns away BEFORE the wall is that close (looks turn at facing.turn_speed).

look.wall_angle.doc: v2.1.1: half-width of the blocked span round the direction to the wall's closest point (the check counts 45; 10 deg margin).

look.min_free_deg.doc: v2.3 (red team #1): a free arc between wall spans narrower than this is no place to look (ClearLook) - it opens and closes as the man moves and his look swings across the walls to it.

look.hold_deg.doc: v2.3 (red team #1): ClearLook hysteresis - the previous result stays a candidate this much better than its distance to the wanted yaw (0 = off, the v2.2 memoryless rule).

look.hold_margin_deg.doc: v2.3: the held look is dropped once a wall direction comes within look.wall_angle minus this of it.

look.narrow_penalty.doc: v2.3 (red team #1): a free arc narrower than look.min_free_deg still competes in ClearLook this much worse (0 = never; < 360 so a narrow arc without a sweep beats a wide one behind a sweep).

look.over_shoulder_max_deg.doc: v2.3 part 7 (user decision 2026-10-26, Q3 = c): on the move a member who is not the rear guard (nor K, nor a fixed look) looks at most this far off the heading - a coverage share in the rear is watched over the shoulder, so he walks forwards (not backwards at move.backward_mult); ClearLook keeps his wall-avoiding look inside it too. 180 = off (v2.2).

look.anticipate_s.doc: v2.3 part 8 (user decision 2026-10-26, Q4 = b): ClearLook also sees the walls from where the man will be this long ahead (his position + velocity x this), so passing a wall end within ~1 m he does not stare at it while its direction swings round. 0 = off.

classify.probe_side.doc: Terrain probe: a wall within this distance to a side marks that side as blocked.

classify.hold_distance.doc: v2: a LOOSER class (open after a wall, a wall after a passage, the other side) takes over only after the leader walked this far with it; tighter classes take over at once. >= the column length (~5 m) so the tail leaves a passage first.

classify.at_wall_dist.doc: v1.2: on ARRIVAL (see classify.arrive_dist) a wall straight ahead within this distance = at_wall (the wall layout).

classify.arrive_dist.doc: v1.2: the leader is arriving when he is within this distance of his move's destination (at_wall only then).

classify.side_ignore_perp_deg.doc: v1.1: the side probes ignore wall segments within this angle of perpendicular to the heading (walls ahead / behind, not beside).

guard.clearance.doc: v2.1: a slot is cut off when the segment from the leader (or a chain neighbour) to it passes closer than this to a wall body (FormationGuardRules.BlockedRoles).

guard.lookahead.doc: v2.1: the guard also checks the formation at the leader's pose this far ahead along his path, so the squad folds before a passage entrance (0 = only where he stands).

turn.fold_deg.doc: v2.1.1 (user 5B): a heading change on the leader's path sharper than this (within turn.lookahead) folds an echelon / line into the trail column for the turn.

turn.lookahead.doc: v2.1.1: how far ahead on the leader's path a sharp turn is looked for (FormationGuardRules.TurnAhead) - ~4.5 s at patrol pace, the time a rear man walking backwards (move.backward_mult) needs to fold an echelon (600 is the least that kept the lab's pace green).

bypass.max_detour.doc: v2.1 (user 2026-10-25): with a known threat the squad passes a wall on the side that hides it from the threat if that path is at most this much longer than the shortest (0.3 = 30 %).

bypass.threat_memory_s.doc: v2.1: a threat seen / heard counts as known for this long after its last contact.

corner.lead_dist.doc: v2.1 slicing the pie: the corner man starts looking round a wall end when the leader is this far (along the heading) before it.

corner.hold_dist.doc: v2.1: ... and keeps looking until the leader is this far past the end.

corner.peek_dist.doc: v2.1: once past the end, he looks at the point this far behind the wall's far face at the end (the area the wall hid).

sight.fov.doc: Vision cone width standing / crouched (checks only; the game owns the real value).
